content:
**cold review caught the fix reintroducing its own defect family (#673)**

**Actor:** fix/issue-673-actor-checks-deny-branch-cannot-report-t (agente)
**Fuente:** issue #673 / PR #693 / plainfiles save on vm

The #673 fix — a deny branch that states what signed evidence it did not evaluate — reintroduced `evidence-reader-empty-on-failure` ONE STATE TO THE LEFT, and its own four-axis mutation round stayed green through it.

WHAT WENT WRONG, and it is the generalizable part: I enumerated three states of the evidence (admissible / non-admissible / absent) and missed the fourth, `decisions === null` = UNCOMPUTABLE. It fell through to the non-admissible branch and rendered as 'A brain-decision/1 block IS PRESENT on this PR but is NOT admissible', instructing an operator who may never have signed anything to go correct a block that may not exist. Reachable BY CONSTRUCTION, not only on failure: gatherActorCheckInputs threads null whenever prNumber does not resolve.

WHY THE MUTATIONS DID NOT CATCH IT — the axis lesson, sharpened: I varied the decisions VALUE axis as {admissible, stale, [], undefined}. `undefined` is a state gatherActorCheckInputs CAN NEVER PRODUCE (both return sites thread the key), while `null` — the state it produces routinely — was never varied. So the axis LOOKED varied and its most-populated value was absent. Next time: derive the value axis from what the PRODUCTION caller can emit, not from what the function signature accepts.

Second blind spot: the remedy sentence had ZERO coverage. Replacing it with nonsense kept 137/137 green. A string that instructs a human is behaviour, and needs a test like any other.

THIRD FINDING, worth remembering on its own: a universal remedy sentence is almost always wrong. 'Re-apply the label as a human AND correct the block' is false in 3 of evaluateSignedDecision's own refusal rules — 11 (head unresolvable), 13 (review author unresolvable), 15 (block is structurally perfect, signed by a review identity, only remedy is a DIFFERENT signer). Rule 15 is one config step from the PR #665 shape the ticket was filed about, so the wrong remedy sent the maintainer around a second loop. The fix defers to the source's own note instead of overriding it.

Also: threading denyActors into evaluateSignedDecision's `.some()` made a non-array value THROW where String#includes had returned a clean fail — and evaluateActor sits OUTSIDE runActorCheck's try/catch. A reporting helper may never convert a verdict into a crash.

CONFIRMS the standing record: brain:review finds nothing; the adversarial cold agent finds everything. It found 3 real defects in code that had 3829/3829 green and 4 mutation axes.

Round 2: 5 mutations, 5 detections, 3832/3832 green. Follow-up #694 opened for a PRE-EXISTING case-sensitivity asymmetry (label deny uses includes/case-sensitive, signature deny case-folds) — a cased login slips the deny gate and is PASSED by the signed-evidence branch.

**Where:** brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs, brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.test.mjs
